crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: GDP Nowcasting
children.blurb: GDP nowcasting is the practice of estimating the current quarter's gross domestic product before the official statistics are published, typically weeks or months ahead of the first government release.

children.name: Reading Central Bank Communication
children.blurb: Reading central bank communication is the quantitative study of what monetary policy statements, minutes, speeches and press conferences reveal about the path of interest rates and the economic outlook.

children.name: Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis
children.blurb: Synthetic populations for policy analysis means building a simulated set of households or firms whose joint characteristics resemble those of a real population, then running tax, benefit or regulatory changes through that simulated population to see who gains and who loses.

children.name: Climate and the Economy
children.blurb: Climate and the economy covers how weather, temperature and the transition away from fossil fuels feed back into output, prices, employment and public finances.

children.name: Agent-Based and Game Theory Models
children.blurb: Agent-based and game theory models in macroeconomic econometrics study economies as populations of interacting decision makers rather than as a single representative agent.

sections.body: Macroeconomic econometrics with AI is the use of machine learning and large scale computation to measure and forecast whole economies. In practice this means models that ingest high frequency data such as payments, shipping, electricity use and job postings to estimate GDP before official figures appear, and language models that parse central bank statements for shifts in tone. It also means building synthetic populations, artificial households and firms calibrated to real survey data, so that policy changes can be simulated before they are tried. Climate work links emissions, weather and physical risk to output and prices. Agent based and game theoretic models simulate many interacting decision makers rather than one representative agent. The common thread is estimation and simulation at the scale of a national or global economy.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Nowcasting works well in normal times and is genuinely useful for tracking turning points, but it struggles at structural breaks such as pandemics or sudden policy shifts, when historical relationships stop holding. Reading central bank communication has moved from simple word counts to contextual models that detect hawkish or dovish signals, yet the mapping from tone to future rate decisions remains noisy and contested. Synthetic populations are credible for tax and transfer questions where survey data are rich, and much weaker for behaviour that depends on trust, credit or informal work. Climate economic models carry large uncertainty about damages, adaptation and tipping points, and their long horizons make validation hard. Agent based models can reproduce stylised facts but are difficult to estimate and to compare against each other. None of this replaces official statistics or judgement, and forecasts from these tools should be read as conditional and revisable.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here divide into measurement, interpretation, simulation and interaction. GDP Nowcasting covers the high frequency estimation problem, what data go in and why revisions happen. Reading Central Bank Communication deals with text and speech as economic data, covering sentiment extraction and the limits of inferring policy intent from language. Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis takes the simulation route, describing how artificial households and firms are constructed and where their behavioural assumptions break down. Climate and the Economy connects physical and transition risk to growth, prices and fiscal positions over long horizons. Agent-Based and Game Theory Models sits underneath several of these, providing the machinery for strategic interaction between many agents. A reader wanting current output estimates starts with nowcasting, one interested in policy signals goes to the central bank page, and one building a simulation should read the synthetic populations and agent based pages together.
